- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon when true values show strong upward momentum; adjust upward for trailing periods.
- When true values show a sharp spike followed by a correction, model tends to overreact and overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-predicts mean price after a strong upward move; adjust downward by 5–10% for periods with sustained high prices.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast forward by 1–2 days for short-term price spikes.
- When true price is consistently above 85, model often overestimates by 5–10%; apply downward correction for high-price regimes.
- For periods with low historical volatility, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 3–5% for low-variance windows.
